## Introduction

`tempoPlot` is a package in the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")` family for
visualizing longitudinal microbiome data. It plots results computed with
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("miaTime")` and `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`.

## Installation

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false

remotes::install_github("0xMuluh/tempoPlot")
```

```{r}
#| label: load

library(tempoPlot)
library(miaTime)
```

## Swimmer plot

`plotSwimmer()` shows when each subject was sampled. In `hitchip1006`, the
subjects followed longest are mostly overweight or obese, while those with
short follow-up are mostly lean.

```{r}
#| label: plot-swimmer

data(hitchip1006)
tse <- hitchip1006
# Some profiles are stored twice; keep the first copy
tse <- tse[, !duplicated(t(assay(tse, "counts")))]
tse <- tse[, tse$subject %in% names(which(table(tse$subject) >= 3))]
plotSwimmer(tse, time.col = "time", group = "subject",
    colour.by = "bmi_group")
```

## Trend plot

`plotTrend()` shows one value over time for each subject: a colData
column, such as a result from miaTime, a feature or an ordination
component. Here, the divergence of each subject from their first sample,
computed with `addBaselineDivergence()`. The subjects were sampled at
different times, so the plot uses visits, the order of each subject's
samples: boxes per visit, with each subject's line drawn over them.

```{r}
#| label: plot-trend

tse <- addBaselineDivergence(tse, group = "subject", time.col = "time",
    assay.type = "counts")
tse$visit <- factor(ave(tse$time, tse$subject, FUN = rank))
plotTrend(tse, y = "divergence", time.col = "visit", group = "subject",
    layout = "box")
```

`baseline` expresses a value relative to each subject's first sample, as a
difference, a ratio or a log2 ratio.

```{r}
#| label: plot-trend-baseline

plotTrend(tse, y = "diversity", time.col = "visit", group = "subject",
    group.by = "sex", baseline = "difference", smooth = "mean")
```
